alignments.note: Rule 31: the article precedes the noun it governs, so it is that noun's determiner and takes *the* together with the supplied relativizer *that*, discontinuously under rule 15, leaving the noun bare — the same division rule 31 makes for τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην → *the righteousness which is from God*, headed on *the*. The modifier is an adverb, not a participle, so there is no verb to carry the relativizer (rules 31-32).
Head noun, bare because the preceding article carries the determiner.

Rule 53: an adverbial predicate carries the supplied copula itself, so *is from above* is the adverb's whole English realization; *from* is part of the adverb's own gloss, not a separate preposition. Head on *above* under rule 17.
The expressed copula of the main clause, the second English *is* (t008); the first (t005) is the supplied one inside the relative clause.

Rule 70: the ASV writes no word for correlative μέν here, so it is its own unrepresented unit. The answering ἔπειτα keeps its own *then*; marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

One Greek adjective rendered by the phrase *easy to be entreated*; the infinitival helper words ride with it under rule 7. Head on *entreated*, the meaning-bearing word realizing the `πειθ-` root, with *easy* answering to the `εὐ-` prefix. The lexeme is a hapax, but rule 91's test is answerable through its two classes and both agree. The `εὐ-` compounds head the stem word and never the prefix word: `εὐάρεστος` → *well pleasing* heads on *pleasing* at 2CO.5.9, EPH.5.10 and PHP.4.18 and → *well pleasing to them* at TIT.2.9, four units and none hedged, 2CO.5.9 saying in terms that *pleasing* carries the sense and *well* is its modifier. The `πειθ-` family heads the root-realizing word throughout its fifteen units — *trust*, *obey*, *persuade*, *confidence* — and spends nothing on a degree or manner word. This is the division rule 84 makes for a privative rendered *without* plus a noun, where the prefix-realizing word is not the head. Heading on *easy* would rest on English syntax alone, which rule 17 refuses.

Genitive complement rendered *of mercy*; rule 17 heads a source noun rendered by *of + noun* on the noun. The single *of* serves both genitives and stays with the first, no Greek preposition being expressed for it to answer to.
Attributive adjective *good*; the ASV reorders it before its noun, which rule 15 permits. Split from καρπῶν under rule 26.
Second genitive complement, bare because the shared *of* stands with ἐλέους.

Rule 84: an alpha-privative adjective rendered *without* plus a noun is one unit headed on the noun, *without* spelling only the privative prefix. The marginal note offers *doubtfulness* or *partiality*, but the text's rendering is what is aligned.
Rule 84 again: *without hypocrisy* headed on *hypocrisy*, the noun glossing the ὑποκρι- root.

review_notes: Returned unchanged: every unit survived review. All 19 source and 27 target ids are partitioned exactly once, every aligned unit has nonempty arrays with both heads inside them, and the one unrepresented unit (s006) has a valid source head and null target head.

s001 is the load-bearing decision and it follows rule 31's precedes-its-noun clause exactly: ἡ … σοφία is the τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην shape, so the article takes the discontinuous *the … that* headed on *the* and σοφία stands bare. The competing reading would leave *that is* on the modifier; rule 31 places the relativizer on the article and rule 53 places only the copula on the adverbial predicate, which is what this unit does. The modifier being an adverb rather than a prepositional phrase changes nothing, since neither has a verb to carry a relativizer.

s003 takes *is from above* whole. *from* is inside ἄνωθεν's own gloss and answers to no Greek preposition, so rule 36 is not in question and the word is not detachable; rule 53's adverbial-predicate clause (ἐγγύς → *were nigh*) puts the supplied copula there rather than on the subject.

The two English *is* tokens are distinguished by position: t005 is the supplied relative-clause copula on s003 and t008 is the expressed ἐστιν. Checked against the target order *that is from above is first pure*.

s012's head is the one materially contested choice and the note names the alternative. εὐπειθής is a hapax, so rule 91's corpus query gives no answer and rule 84's prefix reasoning decides: *easy* realizes εὐ- and *entreated* the πειθ- root, so the root word heads. *easy* is the English phrase's formal syntactic head, which rule 17 forbids as a ground for choosing it.

s006 μέν is the only unrepresented unit, per rule 70's English-side test — the ASV writes no *indeed*, and ἔπειτα's own *then* is not a word for the correlation. A reference comparison will report it as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
The variant line carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark, so rule 97 is not in play and no target token is added; rule 12 forbids revisiting SBLGNT.JAS.3.17.v012 here.
